title: Give employees long service leave
what: Give each employee long service leave (or payment in lieu) once they reach the qualifying period of service, and keep long service leave records.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 2018 (Vic)
sources.publisher: Victorian Legislation (authorised version saved by the owner)
sources.locator: s 6 (authorised version 006, saved by the owner)
sources.quote: At any time after completing 7 years of continuous employment with one employer, an employee is entitled to an amount of long service leave on ordinary pay equal to 1/60th of the employee's total period of continuous employment less any period of long service leave taken during that period.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 2018 (Vic)
sources.publisher: Victorian Legislation (authorised version saved by the owner)
sources.locator: s 37(2) (authorised version 006, saved by the owner)
sources.quote: (2) An employer must keep a long service leave record relating to an employee during the employee's period of continuous employment by the employer.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 2018 (Vic)

sources.quote: (1) The Workforce Inspectorate Victoria may, by instrument, appoint a person employed under Part 3 of the Public Administration Act 2004 as an authorised officer for the purposes of this Act.

reach.note: Every employer of employees in Victoria covered by the Act.

confidence_note: Quoted from the authorised PDF the owner saved from the Victorian register (data/raw/vic_legislation/, not committed); the register's documents disallow automated fetching. Entitlement after 7 years' continuous employment.

assessment.summary: Employers must give long service leave after a long period of service with them. The entitlement builds up with one employer and is mostly lost on moving, which ties workers to employers; it also adds record keeping.

marks.reason: Leave builds up with one employer and is mostly lost on moving, which discourages job changes (unlike portable schemes).

assessment.confidence_note: Marked from the law's design against the framework's guide; no evaluation of state long service leave and job mobility was found.
